stories.title: Rising flour prices fuel weekly inflation
summary: ISLAMABAD: Short-term inflation rose to 11.85 per cent year-on-year in the week ending October 22, driven largely by wheat flour prices, according to official data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) on Friday.

The items whose prices declined week-on-week included tomatoes (21.99pc), petrol (3.63pc), banana (2.42pc), diesel (1.68pc), potatoes (1.38pc), pulse gram (0.93pc), eggs (0.58pc), powdered milk (0.38pc) and broken rice basmati and sugar (0.35pc each).
Last week, short-term inflation rose to 11.38 per cent year-on-year, driven largely by higher food prices, data from PBS showed.

stories.title: UK tells public to keep 3 days' emergency supplies at home following PHP software glitch
summary: The British government advised the public on Friday to keep three days of emergency supplies at home, a message it said had been hammered home by this week’s PHP software glitch, as well as a record-setting summer of heat, drought and wildfires.

The British government said the internet outage showed the importance of its newly launched “Be Ready” campaign, which advises the public to keep three days of bottled water and non-perishable food in the house.
Britain’s advice is similar to that issued by the European Commission, which told EU citizens last year to keep a 72-hour emergency kit containing supplies such as food, water, cash and power banks.

stories.title: Lahore DC gives formal go-ahead for 3-day Basant festivities in March 2027, outlines conditions and restrictions
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore deputy commissioner (DC) on Friday gave the formal go-ahead for three-day Basant festivities in the district from March 12-14 next year, outlining guidelines, conditions and restrictions for the celebrations.
Basant returned to Lahore earlier this year after an 18-year hiatus, with the passing of the Punjab Regulation of Kite Flying Bill, 2025 by the provincial assembly on December 24, 2025.
The notification said the manufacturing of permissible kite-flying material would be allowed from Sept 5, 2026 to March 14, 2027, subject to valid digital registration.

stories.title: R4 ministers' meeting expresses solidarity with Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks
summary: According to a statement by the FO on social media, DPM Dar participated in the sixth R4 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting alongside Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty, and Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud of Saudi Arabia.

Bilateral meetings Dar earlier held bilateral meetings with the Turkish and Egyptian foreign ministers, on the sidelines of the R-4 meeting and a meeting between the R-4 and European diplomats in Istanbul, the FO said.

Separately, DPM Dar met with German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul on the sidelines of the meeting and expressed the desire to further strengthen bilateral ties “through sustained engagement and cooperation across multiple areas of mutual interest”, the FO said.

stories.title: Republican 'Muslim Brotherhood' attacks on Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan seek to exploit Democratic fault lines
summary: Rogers has ​sought to undermine the Democrat’s support among Jewish voters by pointing to El-Sayed’s criticism of Israel’s offensive in Gaza and asserting that El-Sayed has longstanding family ties to the Muslim ⁠Brotherhood.
Strategists said homing in on the Muslim Brotherhood also aims to hurt El-Sayed by exploiting economic tensions between Black voters and Michigan’s large Arab-American community.
Asked about Rogers’ strategy, campaign spokesperson Alyssa Brouillet said El-Sayed’s “extremist positions” on issues ranging from prisons to the Muslim Brotherhood were alienating Michiganders.

stories.title: PM sets indicative wheat price at Rs4,500 per maund for 2027
summary: The PMO statement added that the prime minister’s decision was aimed at “promoting agriculture sector in the country, protecting farmers’ economic interests and increasing wheat production next year”.

Last month, the Pakistan Kissan Ittehad demanded a Rs5,000 per 40kg support price for wheat, warning that farmers may not sow wheat for the next season if the government delays announcing crop policies.

On Oct 13, PM Shehbaz chaired the first National Agricultural and Food Security Council meeting and reaffirmed that the government wanted farmers to get a fair price for wheat and consumers to have affordable wheat.

stories.title: Brent crude hits more than five-month high on concern over Middle East escalation
summary: Oil prices rose on Friday, with Brent crude touching a more than five-month high, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.
Brent crude futures gained $1.40, or 1.2 per cent, to $114.57 a barrel by 1138 GMT (4:38pm PKT), having earlier reached $115 for the highest level since May 4.
US West Texas Intermediate crude gained $1.48, or 1.5pc, to $100.95.

stories.title: Auto illusion
summary: PAKISTAN’S draft auto policy 2026-31 is ambitious in its targets and directionless in its strategy.
The proposed policy aims to generate $6bn in exports over five years, while reducing import tariffs and promoting ‘new’ energy vehicles.
By granting PHEVs a substantial tax advantage, the government is effectively treating vehicles that continue to largely depend on petrol as a preferred route to electrification.

stories.title: At least 12 killed, 22 injured in road accident near Zero Point in Balochistan’s Uthal
summary: KHUZDAR: At least 12 passengers were killed and around two dozen injured when a minibus and a passenger coach collided head-on near Zero Point in Uthal on the Quetta-Karachi Highway in Balochistan on Friday, police said.

A similar accident occurred last month when two people were killed and 15 others injured in a head-on collision between a passenger coach and an LPG bowser near Balochistan’s Kharkhera Customs on the main National Highway in Winder.
In January, four people were killed and several others injured in a road accident near Wadh in Khuzdar district on the Quetta-Karachi National Highway.

stories.title: 10 India-sponsored terrorists killed as bid to undermine state's writ in Gwadar foiled: ISPR
summary: Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Friday that 10 India-sponsored terrorists were killed in separate engagements as security forces thwarted their attempts to “undermine the writ of the state” in Balochistan’s Gwadar district.
The ISPR statement comes a day after security sources said that security forces killed three terrorists and foiled an attack on an unoccupied construction company camp in Gwadar.
Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist activities in recent years, prompting security forces to intensify counter-terrorism operations.

stories.title: State counsel cross-examines prosecution witnesses in security breach case against Imaan, Hadi
summary: ISLAMABAD: A state-appointed counsel on Friday cross-examined all prosecution witnesses in a security breach case against lawyers Imaan Zainab Hazir-Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha.
Anti-terrorism court Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra presided over the hearing held inside Adiala jail on Friday, during which state counsel Atif Mehmood cross-examined a prosecution witness.
During the last hearing, Imaan informed the court that she and Hadi did not need a state counsel as they already had their own lawyers.

stories.title: The Gulf’s emerging web of security partnerships
summary: Its relationship with Saudi Arabia has acquired a more formal security dimension through the 2025 bilateral agreement and the subsequent Makkah framework, while cooperation with Turkiye offers scope for closer military coordination and defense industrial collaboration.
Saudi Arabia is strengthening its relationships with Pakistan and Turkiye while continuing to rely on Western military capabilities and Egypt and exploring defense industrial cooperation with China.

Bahrain remains closely aligned with Saudi Arabia and the GCC defense framework, while Kuwait continues to prioritise bilateral military cooperation with Pakistan alongside its substantial security relationship with Washington.

stories.title: Insulin product in short supply after German manufacturer halts supplies, NA told
summary: An insulin product used by patients with Type 1 diabetes is in short supply in Pakistan after its German manufacturer halted supplies while upgrading its products, Parliamentary Secretary for Health Nelson Azeem said on Friday.

She said the alternatives were at least 20 per cent more expensive and that many patients did not have access to doctors. “Currently, around 34.5 million people in Pakistan have Type 1 diabetes, including children,” she said. “Alternatives are not readily available.

In August 2025, the Pakistan Medical Association raised alarm over “an unprecedented” and severe shortage of essential medicines across the country and warned that the crisis threatened the lives of millions of patients.

stories.title: West Bank attack wounds 5 Israelis as Netanyahu cancels events
summary: An attack in the occupied West Bank wounded at least five Israelis on Friday and triggered a shootout that left two Palestinians dead, prompting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cancel political events days ahead of elections.
No evidence suggests that the Palestinian Authority, the Palestinian government in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, was connected to Friday’s attack.
The incident comes as tensions soar in the West Bank, including over attacks by extremist Israeli settlers against Palestinian olive harvesters, and days ahead of Israeli elections.

stories.title: Apple launches into foldable market as iPhone Duo sales begin
summary: Sales of Apple’s first folding phone, the iPhone Duo, began on Friday, with market watchers betting on whether the device can reinvent the small foldables market in the same way the iPhone did for smartphones.
Within minutes of pre-orders opening last Friday, Apple’s estimated delivery dates for the Duo had slipped to late January as demand outpaced supply.

In China, France, Hong Kong, India and Japan, units would be available only for customers who had ordered online In Sydney, the first Apple store to sell the phones on Friday, a queue of customers formed outside before opening at 8am local time (2100 GMT or 2am PKT).

stories.title: Pakistan, Iran book Billie Jean King Cup final spots
summary: The hosts defeated top seeds Maldives 2-1 in Group A, while Iran secured a convincing 3-0 victory over Qatar in Group B to set up Saturday’s final.
Kuwait claimed the doubles rubber, with Huda and Sumou Aldabbous beating Hajar Al Louzi and Rama Bagaeen 6-2, 6-3.
Pakistan will look to capitalise on home-court advantage when they face Iran in Saturday’s final, with both teams bidding to finish the tournament as Group III champions.

stories.title: Lahore tops global pollution ranking as air quality turns ‘hazardous’
summary: Lahore ranked as the world’s most polluted city on Friday, with its air quality classified as “hazardous”, according to air quality monitoring platform IQAir.
Lahore topped the list of the world’s most polluted cities on Friday morning, with an air quality index (AQI) of 410, according to the IQAir live tracker.
Lahore air quality map. —IQAir The Punjab government’s air quality monitoring platform, meanwhile, recorded an AQI of 339 for Lahore at 11am on Thursday, classifying the air as ‘very unhealthy’.

stories.title: Taiwan shuts down ahead of Typhoon Champi, nearly 1,000 flights cancelled
summary: Almost all of Taiwan shut down on Friday ahead of the arrival of Typhoon Champi, which is forecast to bring strong winds and torrential rain, and though the storm is weakening it could still make direct landfall on the island.

At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of around 191 kph near its centre, according to Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration (CWA).

A fisherman walks among fishing nets at a fishing port as Typhoon Champi approaches Taiwan, in Keelung, Taiwan on October 23, 2026. —Reuters The transport ministry said all 262 domestic flights were cancelled for Friday, along with 717 international ones.

stories.title: FO rejects Indian remarks on OIC Kashmir resolutions, raises alarm over Delhi mosque eviction notice
summary: The two ministers reviewed cooperation under the Regional Four framework, comprising Pakistan, Egypt, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia, and looked forward to the next meeting to strengthen coordination on regional issues.

The spokesperson further outlined Pakistan’s recent diplomatic engagements, including Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu’s state visit from October 20 to 22 at the invitation of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

Also Read: Pakistan, Latvia discuss visa service On the European front, the spokesperson said President Zardari was on an official visit to Germany from October 22 to 24, focusing on strengthening trade, investment and economic cooperation.

stories.title: Sanaullah says letter sent to Achakzai, urges opposition leader to meet PM Shehbaz
summary: Earlier in the day, Achakzai stated that the premier could come to the opposition's office "and have tea with me or give me an invitation and wherever he wants to have negotiations I will go".
The opposition leader added, "Or I can go to him at the prime minister's house and give him an invitation." Achakzai also said, "Discussions will not take place like this.

The opposition had asked the government to ensure that the prime minister personally extended an invitation for negotiations, he said. “Negotiations cannot take place in an atmosphere where the process itself is being mocked,” he said.

stories.title: Brook looks to revive England's campaign
summary: England captain Harry Brook has said his team would return to the drawing board and keep their approach simple as they attempt to revive their campaign in the ODI tri-series after Sri Lanka chased down a target of 430 in a dramatic contest on Thursday.

Sri Lanka pulled off the second-highest successful chase in men's one-day international history, reaching 430-8 with one ball to spare at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium after Brook's record-breaking double century had powered England to 429-4.

Brook struck 202, the fastest double century in men's ODI cricket and the first by an England batsman in the format, but his remarkable innings proved insufficient as Sri Lanka produced a stunning response.

stories.title: Stars reach final after thrilling chase
summary: Stars secured a place in the National Women’s T20 Tournament final with a seven-wicket victory over Invincibles on Friday, while unbeaten Strikers completed their eighth consecutive win by beating Conquerors by 60 runs.
Sadaf Shamas scored an unbeaten 59 and Iram Javed contributed 47 as Stars chased down a target of 141 in 19.2 overs at Bohranwali Ground, finishing on 144-3 with four balls to spare.
Iram’s 47 ensured Stars reached the target and finished level on eight points with Invincibles, advancing to the final on net run rate as their opponents slipped to third place.

stories.title: USEFP opens new gallery space in Islamabad for US exchange alumni artists
summary: The United States Educational Foundation in Pakistan (USEFP), and the Pakistan-US Alumni Network on October 22 opened the first ‘Shahkaar Fankaar Alumni Artist Showcase’ in a new gallery space in the USEFP building in Islamabad, a press release by the US embassy said on Friday.
"This gallery space will feature the achievements of US government-sponsored exchange program alumni in the arts," it said.
The release added that the first exhibition was a solo show by Lahore-based artist Minaa Haroon, an alumna of a US Department of State exchange program on cultural preservation.

stories.title: At least 12 killed as passenger bus collides with van in Balochistan's Uthal
summary: At least 12 people were killed and 22 injured when a passenger bus collided with a passenger van near Zero Point in Uthal, Lasbela district of Balochistan, on Friday, police said.
According to police, the bus was travelling from Lasbela to Karachi when the two vehicles collided near Uthal Zero Point, resulting in heavy casualties.
On October 13, four people were killed and five injured when a passenger van travelling from Quetta to Kalat collided with a truck near Badrang in Mastung district.

stories.title: PCB opens direct signings window for PSL teams, announces pre-season roadmap
summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Friday opened the direct signings window for all eight HBL Pakistan Super League (PSL) franchises and unveiled the pre-season roadmap for the 12th edition of the tournament, which will be held from March 18 to May 2 next year.
PCB Chairman Mohsin Naqvi described the upcoming season as the league’s most ambitious edition yet. “HBL PSL is Pakistan cricket’s biggest stage, and Season 12 will be its most ambitious yet.

We look forward to a season that takes this league further than it has ever gone.” The announcement builds on the landmark 2026 season, when the PSL expanded to eight teams with the inclusion of Hyderabad Kingsmen and Rawalpindiz.

stories.title: China's first AI film hits cinemas, but ticket sales lag
summary: China's first fully AI-generated feature film opens in cinemas on Friday in what promises to be a tough box-office test for the country's booming tech industry as advance ticket sales lag.
"We are the first to try it, the first to get a theatrical release permit, and the first to be tested by the audience," he told Chinese film industry outlet Yuli.

"I think that is not easy at all." Nearly 100 people took more than two years to make the film, which cost more than 10 million yuan ($1.5 million), Bona said, although all the actors, their voices and the backdrops are AI-generated.

stories.title: Security forces kill 10 Indian-sponsored terrorists in Gwadar operations: ISPR
summary: Security forces killed 10 terrorists, including a woman, during operations in Gwadar after Indian-sponsored Fitna al-Hindustan terrorists attempted attacks near the Gabd border crossing and in Gwadar city, the military’s media wing said on Friday.

A day earlier, Radio Pakistan reported that security forces had killed three terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan while foiling an attempt to attack an unoccupied construction company camp in Gwadar.

In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation, which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

stories.title: French, Japanese authors try to write novel on one-day train ride
summary: Sixteen writers -- half French-speaking and half Japanese -- boarded a luxury train in Kyoto on Thursday, faced with the unusual task of collectively writing a novel in under 24 hours.
The authors, who include Muriel Barbery, are taking part in a project by L'ecriture en mouvement -- Writing in Motion -- a French association that promotes literary exchanges.
In the train bar, Toh EnJoe, a master of Japanese science-fiction, sipped a glass of wine as he wrote.

stories.title: Australia sanctions North Koreans over 'fraudulent' IT work, cybercrime
summary: Australia said on Friday it had sanctioned two North Korean individuals and companies over the use of "fraudulent" IT workers and cybercrime to earn cash for the isolated nuclear-armed state.

"The North Korean entities and individuals sanctioned today facilitate North Korea's use of fraudulent IT workers to raise revenue for the regime's nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programmes," the office of Australia's foreign minister Penny Wong said.
Read: North Korea threatens South with 'most horrible' consequences, announces border countermeasures North Korea faces a slew of international sanctions over its weapons and nuclear programmes.

stories.title: LHC acquits Quran desecration convict, cites lack of proof and mental illness evidence
summary: The court held that the prosecution had failed to establish conclusively that the appellant had set fire to the copy.

Also Read: LHC acquits murder convict Examining the evidence, Justice Bajwa noted that the complainant and another key prosecution witness had admitted during cross-examination that they had not seen the appellant setting fire to the copy.
Finding that the prosecution had failed to establish the appellant’s involvement through reliable and consistent evidence, the high court acquitted him by extending the benefit of doubt.

stories.title: New Greece law bans social media for under-15s
summary: Greece's parliament passed a law Friday banning children under 15 from social media, joining a growing number of countries imposing curbs on young people's use of the apps.

Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis announced plans for the ban in April, taking to TikTok — one of the most popular social networks with young people in Greece — to explain the "difficult but necessary" measure.

Read: EU to ban social media for under 13s, curb access until 15 The bill, set to take effect on January 1, will require age verification on social networks and impose harsh penalties if companies fail to comply.

stories.title: Islamabad to get 'Manhattan-style' city, Asia's 'largest safari park': Naqvi
summary: Speaking at the Saudi-Pak Real Estate Expo in Lahore, Naqvi said the auction would start at 15% of the project’s inventory, with investors free to offer a higher share.

Asia's largest safari park planned The interior minister also announced plans for "Asia’s largest safari park, spanning 450 acres in Islamabad," saying the project would tap the country’s potential for entertainment and recreational facilities.

Naqvi further said Islamabad offered significant opportunities for residential and entertainment projects, adding that the government had also taken steps to address concerns over high property prices.

stories.title: Carney says AtkinsRealis is a contender to build nuclear power plant in Turkiye
summary: Canadian engineering company AtkinsRealis is in the running to help build Turkiye's third nuclear power plant, Canadian Prime Minister Mark ​Carney said.

NATO allies Canada and Turkey upgraded their relations to a "strategic partnership" ‌during the first bilateral visit by a Canadian prime minister a day earlier as Carney seeks new global trade partners to reduce reliance on the United States.
Turkiye plans to ​build a second nuclear power plant in the Black Sea region ​of Sinop, ⁠with the third planned in the northwestern region of Thrace.

stories.title: French businesses, events to close with more weekend protests expected
summary: Businesses, cultural events and museums planned to close at the weekend despite curbs on ​demonstrations as French President Emmanuel Macron seeks to restore order a week after nationwide protests turned violent.

Macron blamed "seditious" ultra-left groups for the unrest - allegations the prominent far-left France ​Unbowed party denied - and said a day earlier that "illegitimate" protests would be banned in coming days.

Far-right to meet in Orléans with counter-protests planned All protests planned for Saturday in Marseille and Lyon, France's second- and third-largest cities, have been banned, local authorities said.

stories.title: Utilities in Rawalpindi barred from digging up roads without permission
summary: Commissioner Rawalpindi Salman Ghani issued the directive at a meeting held to review road-cutting permissions and the installation and management of underground utility lines by various government departments.
He said all concerned departments must ensure comprehensive planning and effective coordination before undertaking any road-cutting activity.
All restoration work, including refilling and reconstruction, must be completed within 15 days of road cutting, he said.

stories.title: Proposed amendments to Islamabad LG law cast doubt on Dec 20 polls
summary: The report on the Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government (Amendment) Bill, 2026 (Ordinance No. II of 2026), was presented by committee chairman Raja Khurram Shahzad Nawaz of the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) during Thursday’s session of the National Assembly.
The government introduced the bill in March this year, but the committee’s report was presented a day after the ECP announced the election schedule.

The federal government continued to postpone elections, citing various reasons, including proposed amendments to the Local Government Act, depriving around 2.5 million Islamabad residents of an elected local government system.

stories.title: ATC indicts PAF officer’s murderer, summons witnesses
summary: ISLAMABAD: An Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) on Thursday indicted an accused arrested in connection with the murder of Group Captain Asim Tariq, and summoned prosecution witnesses to record their statements.
Judge Abual Hasnat Mohammad Zulqarnain of the ATC conducted the hearing, during which the accused, Saad Abbasi, was produced before the court.
Police have registered a case against the accused at Margalla Police Station in connection with the murder.

stories.title: Growers critcise PTB for failing to purchase surplus tobacco
summary: The sources said PTB’s role in handling tobacco affairs is critical, but its officials always toe the line of companies, leaving the poor growers high and dry.
However, they said the companies were adopting delaying tactics or were not at all interested in buying the surplus tobacco from growers.
Iqbal Khan Shewa, the association’s patron-in-chief, told Dawn that both companies and traders exploited the weak financial position of tobacco growers.

stories.title: Illegal shops, business centres razed in Charsadda, Lakki Marwat
summary: Also, an anti-encroachment operation has been launched in Tangi tehsil under the supervision of assistant commissioner Akhlaq Ahmad and additional assistant commissioner Adan Zahid to reclaim land.
Traders complained about the operation in Sherpao Bazaar, claiming that their shops were demolished without prior notice, causing them serious financial issues.

Deputy commissioner Shahid Rafiq Gandapur led the operation wherein anti-encroachment squad of the tehsil municipal administration removed illegal buildings and structures from both sides of the busy Peshawar-Karachi Highway in the Serai Gambila Bazaar.

stories.title: Delayed filing of ownership statements: Lahore High Court annuls SECP penalties on mill directors
summary: The SECP had fined each director Rs60,000 under the Securities Act, 2015, for a 253-day delay in filing Form 5 after their re-appointment.
The judge also noted that an SECP clarification of April 20, 2022, indicated ambiguity over whether Form 5 applied to re-appointment of the same directors.
The judge allowed the appeals and set aside the orders of the SECP and its appellate bench.
